principles: Fresh project assets should be declarative and minimal; executable adapter behavior belongs to the global lattice CLI.
Legacy compatibility is a runtime/resolver responsibility, not a reason to keep legacy assets in new projects by default.
Migration commands must be non-destructive unless the user asks for pruning explicitly.
Codex/Claude host conventions should remain thin pointers unless a full asset mode is explicitly selected.
drivers: User wants new projects to stop scattering many Markdown and shim files.
Existing projects must keep working without forced migration.
REVIEW/DONE gates need hard evidence from global commands and smoke tests, not prose claims.

options.name: keep-current-lattice-local-shim-default
cons: Does not answer the user concern
Continues to imply every project needs bin/lattice-codex.js

options.name: global-thin-default-with-legacy-compat
pros: Fresh init becomes clean and product-aligned
Old local shim projects remain supported
Tests can prove both minimal and legacy paths
cons: Requires resolver and adapter check changes
Requires careful managed asset migration semantics

rationale: This option directly satisfies the user-visible clean file tree while preserving old projects and moving executable behavior to global lattice commands.

preMortem.scenario: Fresh init still generates forbidden local shim or .Codex assets.
preMortem.trigger: Init path reuses old wantsCodex/default wrapper branches or managed registry still lists .Codex assets for thin mode.
preMortem.consequence: User still sees the clutter they objected to and the story fails product acceptance.
preMortem.mitigation: Add fresh init smoke with explicit forbidden asset assertions for bin/lattice*.js, .Codex/README.md, .Codex/agents, .Codex/lattice.json and KOALA.md.

preMortem.scenario: Global lattice codex verify fails in a new minimal project because it requires local wrapper heartbeat.
preMortem.trigger: codex-adapter-checks treats missing bin/lattice-codex.js as hard fail for all modes.
preMortem.consequence: Removing local shim breaks the verification workflow and REVIEW/DONE evidence cannot be produced.
preMortem.mitigation: Make local wrapper heartbeat conditional on legacy/full/local-shim assets, and add a smoke that runs global verify/doctor without local bin wrapper.

preMortem.scenario: check --apply deletes or overwrites legacy assets.
preMortem.trigger: Managed asset apply path treats legacy Koala/Codex assets as remove-extra or stale-safe in default mode.
preMortem.consequence: Old projects lose user-edited guidance or wrapper behavior, violating non-destructive migration.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep legacy assets as compatibility/advisory by default; require explicit prune option for deletion and test default non-deletion.

preMortem.scenario: Resolver picks the wrong config when .Lattice and .Codex manifests coexist.
preMortem.consequence: New canonical config is ignored, creating confusing diagnostics and migration drift.
preMortem.mitigation: Set resolver priority to .Lattice/lattice.json first and cover mixed-path cases in legacy smoke.
